A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same agent-memory survey despite the changed title. Their complete text, figures, tables, and references support comparison. Neither contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: Section 3 describes collecting and classifying 218 papers. Figures 3 and 5 report original descriptive analyses of publication trends and memory-category distributions.

after.justification: v4 retains the survey's original analysis of 218 collected papers in Figures 3 and 5. These data-analysis results qualify even though the paper does not conduct model-benchmarking experiments.

M1.justification: The three-dimensional taxonomy remains intact. Expanded descriptions of learned memory management and skill libraries concern surveyed systems; they do not introduce or modify an algorithm proposed by this work.

E1.justification: Both versions describe a 218-paper collection covering 2023 Q1–2025 Q4 and retain the benchmark catalogs. Newly cited benchmarks expand literature coverage, without adding datasets or tasks actually used in the survey's own evaluations.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a proposed method against experimental baselines. Additional systems discussed in v4 are surveyed literature, not newly evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The reported literature-collection procedure and period remain unchanged. Section 7 corrects descriptions of existing metrics, including Recall@K and Pass@K, but does not change an evaluation protocol applied by this work.

E4.justification: The publication-trend and cross-category analyses in Figures 3 and 5 are retained. No ablation, robustness experiment, sensitivity test, or empirical case study is added; the new trade-off table provides conceptual synthesis.

E5.justification: Both versions report descriptive literature counts without repeated-run statistics, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v4 adds no uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: The survey's own numerical results in Figures 3 and 5 are unchanged. v4 newly reports qualitative findings from cited studies, including self-generated skills underperforming human-curated skills (Section 3.2.5) and user-state recovery deteriorating under top-K retrieval (Section 9.6). These are newly summarized findings, not new author-run experiments.

T1.justification: Neither version develops mathematical theorems, proofs, or formal derivations. The expanded memory-hierarchy explanations and revisions to standard metric descriptions do not introduce new formal theory.

C1.justification: The taxonomy, system-design perspective, and real-world utility thesis remain. v4 elevates memory-driven self-evolution into an explicit contribution and expands the abstract's scope to portable, shareable skills and learned context curation, developing themes already present in v1.

C2.justification: v4 substantially develops the interpretation of memory as a loop linking short-term selection, experience consolidation, and skill evolution. Section 3.2.5 adds portable explicit skills as a countertrend to neural internalization and discusses autonomy and security limitations. It also qualifies user/agent category exclusivity and corrects the PersonaMem critique in Section 9.6.

D1.justification: The Figure 3 caption newly explains the counting convention: papers can have multiple cognitive-mechanism labels, while substrate and subject labels partition the collection. This clarifies the existing analysis without establishing a changed procedure. Project and benchmark access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds recent literature including SkillsBench, SkillOps, CoEvoSkills, MemSkill, MemProbe, and InterruptBench, and revises some attributions, including FactScore. These extend existing themes; the central positioning relative to earlier memory surveys remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, memory-subject discussion, and scaling narrative receive substantial rewriting around self-evolving agents. Sections 5 and 6 are reframed and renamed, alongside widespread language corrections and a new title. The overall ten-section organization remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 1 comparing substrate trade-offs across eight dimensions and expands the existing cognitive-memory table. Other tables are retained and renumbered. Figure captions, labels, and some text legibility improve, while the principal diagrams and quantitative plots remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 improves the survey's precision and usability through corrected metric descriptions, a more accurate PersonaMem discussion, clearer classification explanations, and the compact substrate trade-off table. The expanded skills discussion adds useful qualifications about autonomous induction and security. These are worthwhile refinements to the retained taxonomy and descriptive evidence, supporting an incremental overall improvement.
